root_cause.text: In the amd-pstate cpufreq driver, amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init() allocated a cpudata object but failed to release it on the amd_pstate_set_epp() error path, causing a memory leak due to missing cleanup in that failure branch.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit message explicitly says the function "returns with an error code without freeing the cpudata object that was allocated at the beginning of the function," and the patch changes `if (ret) return ret;` after `amd_pstate_set_epp(...)` to `if (ret) goto free_cpudata1;`, adding cleanup before returning.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit message explicitly says the function "returns with an error code without freeing the cpudata object that was allocated at the beginning of the function," and the patch changes `if (ret) return ret;` after `amd_pstate_set_epp(...)` to `if (ret) goto free_cpudata1;`, adding cleanup before returning.

intent_record.intent_summary: Route amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init() EPP setup failures through the cleanup path to avoid leaking cpudata resources.
intent_record.what: In amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init(), the error path after calling amd_pstate_set_epp(policy, cpudata->epp_default) was changed from directly returning ret to jumping to the free_cpudata1 label with goto free_cpudata1 when ret is nonzero.
intent_record.how: On failure of amd_pstate_set_epp(), the function now follows the shared cleanup path instead of exiting immediately, ensuring previously allocated or initialized cpudata-related resources are released before returning the error.

grouping_result.intent: Route amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init() EPP setup failures through the cleanup path to avoid leaking cpudata resources.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it modifies amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init() so that amd_pstate_set_epp() failures go through the cleanup path, preventing the cpudata memory leak from the missing error-branch cleanup.

candidates.rationale: This immediate return on amd_pstate_set_epp() failure exits amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init() without going through the cleanup path, leaking the previously allocated cpudata object.
This conditional guards the faulty error branch; when amd_pstate_set_epp() fails, execution takes the path that returns directly instead of releasing cpudata.

vuln_statements.explanation: This direct return on the amd_pstate_set_epp() failure path exits amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init() before the function reaches its cleanup logic, so the previously allocated cpudata object is not released, causing the memory leak described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of the relevant function `amd_pstate_epp_cpu_init()`, so it is sufficient to assess the leak. The vulnerable construct is present: `cpudata = kzalloc(sizeof(*cpudata), GFP_KERNEL);` allocates memory, and then `rc = amd_pstate_init_perf(cpudata); if (rc) goto free_cpudata1;` and later other failures also go to `free_cpudata1`, but there is a separate error path in the CPPC branch: `ret = rdmsrl_on_cpu(cpudata->cpu, MSR_AMD_CPPC_REQ, &value); if (ret) return ret;` and similarly `ret = rdmsrl_on_cpu(cpudata->cpu, MSR_AMD_CPPC_CAP1, &value); if (ret) return ret;`. These `return ret;` statements occur after `policy->driver_data = cpudata;` and after `cpudata` has been allocated, but they do not free `cpudata`. This shows missing cleanup on an error path after allocation. The root-cause description mentions the `amd_pstate_set_epp()` failure path specifically; in this initial introducing commit there is likewise no cleanup path covering later failures after allocation, and no fix such as calling `kfree(cpudata)` before returning from those post-allocation error branches. Therefore the buggy cleanup behavior is present and the fix is not yet in this function.
